<description>
The `partially_signed_transaction_deserialize` target feeds raw bytes to the PSBT parser. Byte-level mutations rarely produce well-formed key-value maps with valid keydata (pubkeys, xpubs, control blocks, DER signatures, etc), so most inputs are rejected early and the deeper per-field parsing is rarely reached.

This PR adds a custom mutator for PSBT which is ported from bitcoinfuzz (with some changes).  The mutator splits the input into global/input/output maps of key-value records, applies the mutations and serializes the result again. The first commit is a preparation to allow targets to provide a custom mutator by adding an optional `mutator` field to
`FuzzTargetOptions`.

note: LLM assisted on porting the custom mutator.
</description>

[2026-11-03] rc:4460347597 inline on CMakeLists.txt by ekzyis (contributor) (edited 2026-11-03):
I don't know how much we care about honggfuzz, but honggfuzz has a similar problem. [It also defines `LLVMFuzzerMutate`](https://github.com/google/honggfuzz/blob/940b958dfeb6f9131fd846cae31fcc0fe996ae98/libhfuzz/libhfuzz.h#L32) and throws a warning because of `-len_control=100` (no crash like AFL++). See reproduction which simulates appending `-len_control=100` to argv like `restore_default_len_control()` would do:

```
$ hfuzz-clang++ -std=c++20 argv.cpp -o argv
$ echo hello > seed
$ ./argv < in/seed
[2026-11-03T15:07:11-0600][W][31466] HonggfuzzRunFromFile():80 Cannot open '-len_control=100' as input, using stdin: No such file or directory
Accepting input from '[STDIN]'
Usage for fuzzing: honggfuzz -P [flags] -- ./argv
TestOneInput size=6
```

```cpp
// argv.cpp
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdio>
#include <vector>
extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerInitialize(int* argc, char*** argv)
{
    static char len_control_arg[]{"-len_control=100"};
    static std::vector<char*> g_argv;
    g_argv.assign(*argv, *argv + *argc);
    g_argv.insert(g_argv.begin() + 1, len_control_arg);
    g_argv.push_back(nullptr);
    *argc = g_argv.size() - 1;
    *argv = g_argv.data();
    return 0;
}
extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t* data, size_t size)
{
    printf("TestOneInput size=%zu\n", size);
    return 0;
}
```

Claude suggested a configure-time opt-in. Then we wouldn't need to detect the engine and rewrite arguments, but the custom mutator would be off by default and I think if there's a custom mutator available, we never want to run without it. Sounds like a good trade-off to me, though.
